filo delete [DIR] [-y]

  Lists the files past their retention under DIR (inside a root), or under every
  root, whose content has not changed since the retention was set, and the
  duplicate copies marked for deletion (see filo help update) with the copies
  kept, then asks: all, select one by one, list them all, or none [a/s/l/N]. In
  a terminal the list shows 10 entries per section; l lists every one. Select
  goes file by file: d delete, r new retention, s skip or q quit; for a
  duplicate copy, u unmark in place of r. Enter, or an answer filo does not
  know, never deletes anything. Without a terminal it only lists. Deletion is
  permanent: there is no recycle bin, so keep backups.

Flags
  -y                       delete them all without asking

  A duplicate copy is deleted only after another copy of the same content has
  been read again and found unchanged at its path, and only if that copy is kept
  at least as long; otherwise its group is skipped. The last copy of a content
  is never deleted this way.

  Just before deleting, each file is read again. It is deleted only if it is
  still at its path as the same file and its content is still the content its
  retention was set on; otherwise it is skipped with one line saying why. A file
  that cannot be read is never deleted. Folders the run emptied are removed, up
  to the root. Exit code 1 if a file could not be read or deleted.
